s: West Africa's biggest single market, 50,000 shoppers a day
w: Eight thousand stalls, twenty thousand vendors, and roughly fifty thousand shoppers pushing through every single day -- Kejetia is the largest single market in West Africa, and Kumasi's beating commercial heart since long before anyone thought to count.
_facts: open-air marketplace in Kumasi, Ashanti Region, Ghana
over 8,000 stores and stalls, largest single market in West Africa
about 50,000 people visit daily, 20,000 vendors operate there

s: Ghana's largest Methodist church, named for John Wesley
w: The largest Methodist church in the region anchors the Adum episcopal area, named for the movement's founder. A century of Sunday mornings has passed through these doors -- still the center of Methodist life in the Ashanti capital.
_facts: largest Methodist church in the area, center of the episcopal area in Adum, Kumasi
named after John Wesley, one of the founders of the Methodist church

s: A museum built to honor the Asantehene who returned
w: Opened in 1954 inside the Centre for National Culture, this museum is named for Prempeh II, the Asantehene whose jubilee it marks. Artifacts of Ashanti royal history sit under one roof, a short walk from the palace they came from.
_facts: museum located in Kumasi, Ghana, established in 1954
located in the Centre of National Culture
named after and features artifacts related to Prempeh II

s: The minor basilica seat of Kumasi's Catholic archdiocese
w: Dedicated in 2004, this Catholic basilica serves as the seat of the Archdiocese of Kumasi -- a modern landmark in a city otherwise defined by centuries-old Ashanti institutions. New enough to still smell like fresh stone.
_facts: Roman Catholic cathedral and minor basilica dedicated to Saint Peter
seat of the Archdiocese of Kumasi

s: Everyone still calls it Kumasi Fort
w: Everyone still calls it Kumasi Fort, though its official name is the Armed Forces Museum. Established in 1953 inside the old colonial garrison, it holds Ghana's military history behind fortress walls built for an entirely different war.
_facts: military history museum located in Kumasi, Ghana, also known as Kumasi Fort

s: The Ashanti royal palace built after a war took the old one
w: Built in 1925 as Asantehene Prempeh I's home after decades of exile, Manhyia Palace replaced the residence lost in the Yaa Asantewaa war. Its museum now holds Ashanti royal history, including artifacts on loan from the British Museum -- returned, for now.
_facts: historical museum in Kumasi, situated within Manhyia Palace
first established 1925 as private residence for Asantehene Agyeman Prempeh I after his exile, built as compensation for the palace destroyed at Adum during the Yaa Asantewaa war of 1900
32 Asante artefacts loaned to the museum by the British Museum and Victoria and Albert Museum in 2024
